role.altitude: The boiler operator keeps walking rounds, testing water, judging readings, deciding adjustments, fixing problems on the spot and signing the log; reading chart recorders, checking tank levels by eye, searching paper logs for history and copying readings into the log shrink.
reach: Plant users of steam and power
role.ambitious_version: An operator who sees a boiler drifting from the trend before an alarm, and whose log fills itself during the shift.

tasks.short: Test boiler water, check chemical and fuel tank levels, decide adjustments, and make adjustments to dosing and blowdown to maintain required levels.

steps.what: Boiler operator samples and tests boiler water: conductivity, pH and hardness
Boiler operator checks chemical and fuel tank levels on rounds
Boiler operator decides adjustments to dosing and blowdown
Boiler operator makes adjustments to maintain required water, chemical and fuel levels

tasks.design: Online analysers on the main boilers measure conductivity and pH continuously and show them on the control screen, so the operator tests these by hand less often and still tests hardness and phosphate. Level transmitters on chemical and fuel tanks show levels with low-level alarms, and rounds still check for leaks. Deciding and making adjustments stay with the operator; no software doses. Recording values belongs to the daily log task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every value needed a hand test or a look at a sight glass.
tasks.enabler_now: Online water analysers and tank level transmitters on the control screen.
tasks.still_hard: Analysers that drift without anyone noticing.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing foaming or carryover before the numbers show it.

ambition.what: Adjust dosing on continuous values instead of a few tests a shift.

reach.learn: Whether continuous values cut chemical use.

evidence.claim: AI acting as a safety component in supplying heat or electricity is high-risk; dashboards and readings are not.
Online analysers and level transmitters feed control screens in boiler houses.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and adjusting levels; recording values (task 10476) and weighing fuel (task 10482) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: online analysers installed and calibrated by the instrument team on the main boilers, about 60% of test effort; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: level transmitters on chemical and fuel tanks wired to the control system.
Deciding and adjusting keep their full time.

incremental.description: Boiler operator checks analysers against a hand test each day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small boilers without analysers; high: main boilers with analysers and level transmitters.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather trends and alarm history, inspect the equipment, analyze problems and decide action, and take appropriate action to keep equipment and systems running.

steps.what: Boiler operator gathers trends and alarm history around the problem
Boiler operator inspects the equipment on site
Boiler operator analyzes problems and decides the appropriate action
Boiler operator takes action: adjusts, switches to standby or fixes minor faults

tasks.design: A trend view in the historian shows the values and alarm history around the problem on one screen, instead of reading paper chart recorders and leafing back through the log. Inspecting, analysing and acting stay with the operator. Logging the malfunction and calling manufacturers are sibling tasks and are priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: History sat on paper charts and in handwritten logs.
tasks.enabler_now: Historian trend views with alarm history.
tasks.still_hard: Faults that start outside the measured values.

reach.learn: Whether trend views speed up repairs.

evidence.claim: A shift handover product links sensor data and field notes to the plant historian.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing and acting on problems; logging malfunctions (task 10476) and contacting manufacturers (task 10485) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: the historian, run by the instrument team, stores boiler values and alarms.
Inspecting, analysing and acting keep their full time.
unknowns: How many values the historian holds.
research_questions: Is time to restore operation shorter?

incremental.description: Boiler operator reports missing values in the trend view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: problems found on rounds; high: problems that need history to explain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk rounds reading local gauges, read control screens and charts, observe and interpret readings registering boiler operation, and report abnormal readings.

steps.what: Boiler operator walks rounds and observes local gauges and meters
Boiler operator reads chart recorders and control screens
Boiler operator interprets readings registering boiler operation to judge whether boilers operate properly
Boiler operator reports abnormal readings to the shift supervisor

tasks.design: Pressures, temperatures, flows and flue gas values that already have transmitters are shown on one overview with limits and historian trends, replacing paper chart recorders, so rounds focus on gauges without transmitters and on what can only be seen, heard or smelled. Interpreting readings and reporting stay with the operator. Recording readings belongs to the daily log task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were on local gauges and paper chart recorders.
tasks.enabler_now: Control overviews with limits and historian trends.
tasks.still_hard: Gauges that stick or read wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a smell or sound no instrument registers.
tasks.altitude: Fewer gauges to read; judging stays.

reach.learn: Whether abnormal readings are reported earlier.

evidence.claim: At a large chemical site 650,000 readings from digital rounds reached the historian in one year; no time saving reported.

assumptions: Boundary: observing and interpreting readings; recording them (task 10476) and inspecting equipment for faults (task 10474) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1 and s2: transmitters on about 60% of the round's readings, wired to the control system and historian; s1 and s2 are priced at that share.
Interpreting and reporting keep their full time.

incremental.description: Boiler operator compares a sample of screen values with local gauges each week.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older boiler houses with few transmitters; high: 60% of readings transmitted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record instrument readings, test results, malfunctions and maintenance work, and safety tests to maintain daily logs of operation, maintenance and safety activities, and review and sign the shift log.

steps.what: Boiler operator records instrument readings in the daily log
Boiler operator records water test results
Boiler operator records details of equipment malfunctions and maintenance work
Boiler operator records safety activities: safety valve, low-water cutoff and alarm tests
Boiler operator reviews and signs the shift log for handover

tasks.design: The electronic log takes transmitted readings from the historian at set times, and gauges without transmitters are entered on a rounds handheld with limits. Water test results come from the online analysers or are entered on the handheld. Malfunctions and maintenance are logged with an equipment tag and a fault pick list that links to the maintenance work order. Safety tests are ticked on a checklist with time stamps. The operator reviews and signs the shift log. Log entries show who did what; any use beyond the log is agreed with the works council first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper logbooks and spreadsheets filled by hand every hour.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic logs fed by the historian and rounds handhelds.
tasks.human_edge: Writing the remark that tells the next shift what to watch.

ambition.what: Review drifts across shifts weekly instead of only when something fails.

tasks.altitude: Much less writing; review and signature stay.

reach.learn: Whether test records are complete at inspection.

evidence.claim: A mining plant replaced spreadsheet logsheets with historian-based logsheets and reported more than 1,500 hours a year freed; vendor case without method.
Logs and rounds record who did what and when and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping the daily log; weighing and recording fuel (task 10482) and accident reports (task 10491) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: the historian holds about 70% of the logged readings; the rest are entered on the rounds handheld; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: online analysers on the main boilers from task 10472; other tests entered on the handheld.
Review and signature keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of logged readings with transmitters.

incremental.description: Boiler operator reports wrong tag mappings in the electronic log.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older boiler houses with few transmitters; high: 70% of readings from the historian.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
